name: Pottiaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the source Tortella squarrosa concept at family level through robust acrocarpous turf, strongly crisp/contorted dry leaves that spread squarrose-recurved when wet, a strong costa and papillose distal cells, while preserving the unresolved North American species-level Pleurochaete/Tortella conflict.

project_scope.selection_mode: Source Tortella squarrosa retained as provenance; species promotion deliberately pending
project_scope.note: WFO recognizes Tortella squarrosa globally in Pottiaceae, but FNA's North American Pleurochaete treatment excludes P. squarrosa sensu stricto from the New World and routes the New World squarrosa-like facies to Pleurochaete luteola. Texas material therefore needs specimen/microscopic review before a current species concept is promoted.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Wet and dry the moss. The source squarrosa-type plant has long leaves that twist/crisp strongly when dry and spread or bend backward squarrose-recurved when moist.
family_diagnostics.gametophyte: Acrocarpous robust moss forming coarse turfs on calcareous or dry mineral substrates in the squarrosa-type concept.
family_diagnostics.leaf_anatomy: Leaves have a strong costa; distal laminal cells are papillose. In the FNA Pleurochaete concept, hyaline basal marginal cells form distinct clear strips rather than the V-shaped basal border typical of true Tortella.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Pottiaceae commonly has terminal or lateral gametangia and capsules with family-level peristome variation; species-level reproductive placement is important in the Pleurochaete/Tortella distinction.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Crisp-dry / squarrose-wet acrocarp + strong costa + papillose upper cells = Pottiaceae-level source concept; stop before species unless basal-cell and reproductive details are checked.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: dry-vs-wet habit → strong costa → papillose cells → basal hyaline band → reproductive position → Tortella/Pleurochaete taxonomy caution
visual_lesson.intro: This is a good example of where a visual learner should know exactly when to stop. The field habit is useful for Pottiaceae, but the Texas source name cannot safely be promoted to species without microscopic characters.

steps.title: 1 · Photograph the same turf dry and wet
steps.look_for: Dry leaves strongly contorted/crisp and hugging or twisting around the stem; wet leaves spreading and recurving outward in a squarrose posture.
steps.why_it_matters: This motion/shape change is the most memorable source-concept cue.

steps.title: 2 · Find the strong costa
steps.look_for: A conspicuous central costa extending through most or all of the leaf.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates the source concept sharply from ecostate Leucodon.

steps.title: 3 · Zoom into the upper cells
steps.why_it_matters: Papillose upper cells are a useful Pottiaceae microscopic confirmation.

steps.title: 4 · Inspect the clear basal margins
steps.look_for: Hyaline elongated cells forming clear strips along the basal leaf margins.
steps.why_it_matters: FNA uses the geometry of these basal cells to separate Pleurochaete from Tortella.

steps.title: 5 · Do not skip reproductive position
steps.look_for: Whether reproductive structures are terminal or lateral relative to the main shoot.
steps.why_it_matters: Pleurochaete's lateral reproductive architecture is one reason FNA separates it from Tortella.

steps.title: 6 · Preserve the taxonomy conflict visibly
steps.look_for: Source: Tortella squarrosa. WFO recognizes that name globally. FNA: North American squarrosa-like plants → Pleurochaete luteola; P. squarrosa s.str. excluded from New World.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents an uncertain Texas specimen from being silently converted into a false canonical ID.

comparisons.title: Pottiaceae vs Leucobryaceae
comparisons.rule: The source Pottiaceae concept has ordinary green leaves with strong costa and papillose cells, dramatically crisping when dry. Leucobryum has a pale leaf dominated by a multilayered leucocyst-rich costa.

comparisons.title: Pottiaceae vs Leucodontaceae
comparisons.rule: The source Pottiaceae concept is acrocarpous and costate; Leucodon is pleurocarpous with cylindrical appressed-leaf branches and no costa.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not promote the Texas source Tortella squarrosa to a settled current species from field appearance. WFO and FNA disagree in a way that materially affects New World identification; retain the source label and require microscopic/specimen review.

genera.fast_cue: source label only; crisp-dry/squarrose-wet costate pottioid moss

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: WFO currently recognizes Tortella squarrosa globally in Pottiaceae.
WFO also retains Pleurochaete squarrosa in Pottiaceae, reflecting competing nomenclatural/taxonomic treatments.
FNA excludes P. squarrosa s.str. from the New World and treats New World squarrosa-like material as P. luteola. Texas source needs microscopic/specimen reconciliation.
